text:
The man will likely prevail. The recorded easement was extinguished by merger when he acquired the woman's house, since he then held both the dominant and servient estates, and recording did not preserve it. His later warranty deed could not revive the easement or pass an interest he no longer held, and the path offers only a more direct route, not a necessary one, so an implied easement is unlikely. The shared note is wrong to say the recorded easement passed with the house.

CONFIDENCE: 70
